en: The Therāpadāna:
The Chapter on the Vibhītaka Tree, 2.
The Apadāna of the Elder Koladāyaka
“At that time, clothed in an antelope skin and wearing a garment of bark,
having filled a cartload [of provisions],”
I was a resident of my hermitage at Kolaṃhāsi.
At that time, the Buddha Sikhī was alone and without a second.
Knowing [the truth] for all time, he approached my presence;
having gladdened his own mind, he came.
Having paid homage to the one of excellent vows,
I took a jujube fruit with both hands and gave it to the Buddha.
In the thirty-first aeon from now,
because I gave that fruit back then,
I have not known a miserable rebirth.
This is the fruit of giving kola-fruit:
the defilements within me have been incinerated... [and so on].
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [and so forth].
The Buddha’s teaching has been proclaimed:
the four analytical knowledges, and so forth...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the Venerable Elder Koladāyaka recited these verses.
This is the second legend (apadāna) of the Elder Koladāyaka.
